To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a decrease of ≥ 2 h sleep per night was found to be associated with a higher incidence risk of metabolic syndrome.
a change in self-reporting sleep duration is associated in a dose-response fashion with metabolic syndrome.
(i) a decrease of ≥ 2 h sleep duration per night is associated with an increased risk of metabolic syndrome (Met S); and (ii) persistent short sleepers also had an increased risk of incident Met S.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between sleep duration change and metabolic syndrome.
the effect of sleep duration on MetS incidence.
the effect of sleep duration changes on MetS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sleep duration should be considered as a potential modifiable factor for MetS prevention.
short sleep duration, especially when it decreases ≥2 hours per night, is associated with an increased risk of developing MetS.

a short or long sleep duration is associated to a higher risk of MetS, and the association of sleep duration with incident MetS was stronger among individuals with an increase of ≥2 hours sleep per night.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
short sleepers are at an increased MetS risk, and the risk of MetS is further enhanced by a decrease in sleep duration.

a reduction in sleep duration of ≥2 hours per night is associated with an increased risk of metabolic syndrome, and that short sleep duration is also associated with an increased incidence of metabolic syndrome.
sleep deprivation is associated with MetS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sleep duration is an important modifiable risk factor for MetS.
a reduction of ≥2 hours in sleep duration may be an independent risk factor for the development of metabolic syndrome.

sleep duration is a modifiable factor that can be used to reduce the risk of MetS, and therefore, public health interventions that promote adequate sleep duration may be beneficial for reducing the prevalence of MetS.
